proof_attempt_summary: The run developed the Gaussian sparse-drift interval program, a finite-radius affine shortening argument, a canonical sparse-versus-convexified numerical witness, and deterministic epsilon-approximation. D0.5 stopped at the field floor with an incremental forecast and an unsalvageable-in-scope ceiling. The strong-duality and raw-data-transfer arguments retain load-bearing proof gaps; this bank is a research record, not an established theorem or a soundness certificate.
tldr: Weak cross-trial drift cannot be removed by compatibility selection at root-sample-size scale. The raw finite-stratum trial is reduced to an independent Gaussian location coordinate and noisy drift contrasts, and the exact local minimax expected length of connected uniformly honest intervals is characterized by an interval-constrained strong dual. A terminating discretization supplies continuum-valid upper and lower certificates and transfers back to the raw experiment. In the canonical three-stratum design, the finite rational radius \(B=300000\) has the certified strict comparison \(L_G\le7.833522<7.839521\le L_{\mathrm{conv}}\le L_{\mathrm{aff}}\), proving that sparse face geometry can yield a genuine nonlinear borrowing gain.
gap: External-control methods obtain efficiency under exchangeability or select compatible controls under beta-min separation. Decision theory covers arbitrary confidence sets, nonconvex expected-length rates, or affine Gaussian intervals, but not the exact connected-interval constant under weak sparse drift.
fill: The project proves a connected-interval Gaussian primal--dual equality, constructs certified continuum-valid approximations, and uses an explicit rescaling and invariantization map to prove matching lower and upper transfers for uniformly honest raw-data intervals. Exact symmetric Gaussian calibration supplies a strict borrowing gain at each fixed finite radius, with no radius-uniform gap claimed.
